instantiated_cells.justification: The statute requires lobbyists meeting the threshold to file bi-monthly reports, not annual spending reports by lobbyists.
The required lobbyist spending report cadence is bi-monthly, not monthly.
Lobbyists must file a 'bi-monthly written report' on a schedule of six two‑month reporting periods, which is an 'other' cadence.
Reporting periods are defined as two-month periods (Jan–Feb, Mar–Apr, etc.), not quarterly.
Semi-annual spending reports are filed by the client, not by the lobbyist as the named filer of a separate spending report.
The statute establishes bi-monthly reporting periods rather than three times per year tied to a legislative calendar.

cell.value: Bi-monthly (six reporting periods: Jan–Feb, Mar–Apr, May–Jun, Jul–Aug, Sep–Oct, Nov–Dec; due the 15th day after each period).

instantiated_cells.justification: Section 1-h(a) defines six two-month reporting periods and sets the due date as the 15th day next succeeding the end of each period.
Lobbyists must report expenses and itemize those over $75 by amount, payee, and purpose (with aggregate reporting allowed for $75 or less).
Lobbyists required to report must file bi-monthly spending reports (every two months), which is an 'other' cadence than the listed options.
The bi-monthly lobbyist report must list general subjects and legislative bill numbers and other executive/agency actions lobbied.
Lobbyists must disclose 'the compensation paid or owed to the lobbyist' in their bi-monthly reports.
The lobbyist report requires identification of the person/organization/body lobbied before but does not require disclosure of specific contacts or communications.
Expenses are reported overall and itemized by amount/payee/purpose above $75, but the statute does not require expenditures to be broken out per issue.
The bi-monthly report must include 'a description of the general subject or subjects' on which the lobbyist has lobbied.
Lobbyists must disclose general subjects of lobbying in their bi-monthly reports.

Because 'expenses' are defined broadly as expenditures incurred for lobbying and must be reported and itemized above $75, the report encompasses costs such as gifts/entertainment/transportation/lodging to the extent they are lobbying expenses (though personal sustenance/lodging/travel of the lobbyist is excluded).
The report requires disclosure of lobbying expenses (other than specified exclusions) and allows aggregation for certain salary expenses, capturing non-compensation/indirect costs.
Lobbyists file bi-monthly reports that include their name, client, issues/bill numbers, and compensation paid/owed plus lobbying expenses with itemization rules.
The lobbyist bi-monthly report must include the lobbyist's name, address, and telephone number.

Lobbyists must report legislative bill numbers and numbers/subject matters of executive orders and other actions lobbied, satisfying disclosure of specific actions influenced (though not position taken).
The lobbyist report requires the client's name, address, and telephone number but does not require stating whether the principal is public or private or describing the principal's business.
The bi-monthly report must include the client's name, address, and telephone number.

Registration and bi-monthly reporting require identifying the client by whom the lobbyist is retained/employed/designated, and a separate registration is required for each client, effectively disclosing all represented principals.
The lobbyist bi-monthly report must include 'the legislative bill numbers of any bills' on which the lobbyist has lobbied.
The bi-monthly report requires disclosure of 'the compensation paid or owed to the lobbyist,' i.e., direct lobbying costs.
Lobbyists must report 'any expenses expended, received or incurred' for lobbying, which provides total lobbying expenditures/expenses (with certain exclusions) for the period.
Lobbyists must file itemized spending reports including employer/client identification, issues and bill numbers, and compensation and expenses.
Expenses over $75 must be detailed by amount, payee, and purpose (itemized format), even though smaller expenses may be aggregated.

unscoreable_emissions.reason: The provided sections specify who must file and what must be included, but do not state whether a lobbyist with zero activity/spending must file a 'no activity' report.
While gifts to spouses/children are prohibited in § 1-m, the provided reporting provisions (§ 1-h) do not expressly require reporting spending on household members of public officials.
